user: What is the purpose of Endianness?
assistant: Endianness is a concept that indicates how bytes of data are organized by the underlying computer architecture. There are two types of endianness: big-endian, which orders data by most-significant bit, and little-endian, which orders data by least-significant bit. In the context of the Speech to Text service, the service automatically detects the endianness of the incoming audio. However, for the audio/l16 format, you can specify the endianness to disable auto-detection if needed.

* How do I convert my text to speech?

To submit text to the service for synthesized audio output, you make an HTTP or WebSocket request. You can use the API directly or use one of the Watson SDKs.

There is no graphical user interface for submitting text. See the [Text to Speech demo](https://www.ibm.com/demos/live/tts-demo/self-service/home) to try an example of the service in action.

If your domain was added when the default SSL mode was End-to-end Flexible, that setting is not overwritten. You can change the mode to a less strict mode, but that is not recommended for production environments.

 What is DDoS?

A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack is an attempt to make an online service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic from multiple sources. In a DDoS attack, multiple compromised computer systems attack a target such as a server, website, or other network resource, affecting users of the targeted resource.

The flood of incoming messages, connection requests, or malformed packets to the target system forces it to slow down or even crash and shut down, thereby denying service to legitimate users or systems. DDoS attacks have been carried out by diverse threat actors, ranging from individual criminal hackers to organized crime rings and government agencies.

A higher rate causes the text to be spoken more quickly; a lower rate causes the text to be spoken more slowly. The parameter changes the per-voice default rate for an entire request.

 The speaking pitch represents the tone of the speech that the service synthesizes. It represents how high or low the tone of the voice is perceived by the listener. A higher pitch results in speech that is spoken at a higher tone and is perceived as a higher voice;
